description:
Step of fz-t93, after fz-t93.20 (T1, merged #625). Page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-t93.22.html (pending). Research: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/t93_22/r/report.md and r/b/report.md.

Finding (develop daf7278c4, distiller): the drain re-certifies the same cone each round. 8 certifications; certs 4-7 certify 11.8k-12.7k outputs each (48.2k together), of which 1.8k are first-time and none moved revision. Repeated work (revoke wave + re-grant + dispatch of readiness changes) costs ~661M, 5.1% of the run: the ceiling of any certificate design.

Mechanism (measured): not the wake path (a woken waiter's claims are already unquiet: 0 wave pops). Each repeat follows exactly one first-run AnalyzeActivation of a newly discovered activation. Its completion claims facts already published and quiet without changing their revision (NameableModules and Raisable via an unconditional outputs.extend in jobs/semantic.rs analyze_activation; and callee Activation(f)/ActivationInputs(f)), and the post-run quiet-flip wave unquiets the whole cone reading them. The revocation is legitimate (fz-229, fz-afu.15 S1-S5): a publisher that may still contribute holds the fact unfinal. The waste is O(cone) revoke and re-grant per round.

Probes (n=3 interleaved, clean base, stdout identical): batch-certify / unsorted wave ~0 (per-fact eager finality is the cost, not its organization). Claiming NameableModules/Raisable only when raises_of is non-empty: -0.64%, repeats unchanged (callee re-claims remain), derivations pin 18_335 -> 18_336, wakes change.

Design candidate: lazy certificate (quiet derived from a certificate's validity; revoke O(1), re-grant O(delta)); paper in r/report.md section 4, unprobed, changes the data model and the settled-bit event invariant. Bar: byte-identical output, wakes unchanged, pin falls lowered, rises to the user.
title: A certified cone stays certified until a read enters it or a publisher in it moves
